noticeTitle: Rebind isn’t notarized by Apple yet
noticeDescription: Notarization needs a paid Apple Developer ID, which the project doesn’t have yet. Rebind is signed and its code is open, but on first launch macOS says it can’t verify the app. You only need to allow it once, using either option.

heroTitle: Make every key, button and tap
heroLead: Rebind remaps keys, mouse buttons and trackpad gestures to shortcuts and macOS actions, and keeps running quietly from the menu bar.
devicesTitle: One app for every input device
devicesLead: Your keyboard, mice, the built-in trackpad, Magic Trackpad and Magic Mouse each get their own bindings.
experimental: Trackpad and Magic Mouse gestures are experimental: macOS keeps its own gestures on, so it may react to the same tap too.
actionsLead: Press, double press or hold. Send a shortcut, move a window, open an app or run an Apple Shortcut.
triggersDescription: Keys, mouse buttons, the wheel and touches, with Command, Control, Option and Shift.
actionsDescription: A shared catalog for every device, from shortcuts to windows and media.
profilesDescription: Named profiles for work, games or editing. Switch from the menu bar or with a binding.
perAppDescription: A binding for one app replaces the general one there. Exclude games and virtual machines entirely.
scrollingDescription: Reverse vertical and horizontal scrolling separately, speed up the wheel and set smooth scrolling for each mouse.
logitechDescription: SmartShift, DPI, high-resolution scrolling, battery level and the gesture button on supported models.
backupsDescription: Rebind keeps your last 10 configurations automatically. Export one profile or a full backup.
menuBarDescription: A visible paused state, launch at login and an emergency pause shortcut.
privacyLead: Rebind asks for Accessibility access to read and send input. Bluetooth access is optional and only used for mouse battery levels.

faqQ1: Why does macOS say it can’t verify Rebind?
faqA1: Rebind is signed and open source but isn’t notarized yet. Allow your downloaded copy once using either option in the installation guide above.
faqQ2: Does Rebind see what I type?
faqA2: Rebind checks key presses only to match your bindings. It doesn’t collect typed text, passwords or the clipboard. Input data stays on your Mac.
faqQ3: Can I remap Caps Lock or Fn?
faqA3: Not in the current version. Caps Lock, Fn/Globe, modifier-only triggers and left/right modifier distinctions aren’t supported.
faqQ4: Are trackpad and Magic Mouse gestures stable?
faqA4: They’re experimental and use a private macOS interface. Native gestures remain active and may react to the same tap. Keyboard and conventional mouse bindings aren’t affected.
faqQ5: Does it work alongside Logi Options+?
faqA5: Rebind works with supported Logitech mice on its own. Logi Options+ or G HUB may take control of the mouse; Rebind shows a warning when either is running.
faqA6: Rebind checks for signed updates with Sparkle once a day, or when you choose Check for Updates, and asks before installing them.
